title: Behavioural and physical activation for multimorbid older patients with depressive symptoms during inpatient-outpatient transition
summary:
Depressive disorders in old age are common, especially in older adults living at home and inpatients in geriatrics and geriatric psychiatry.  Depressive disorders in old age are often under-diagnosed and under-treated, with negative consequences for the patient's health. Older people living at home with multiple illnesses have particularly poor mental health care and are at risk of being hospitalised more often. There is a lack of programmes to consolidate treatment gains and prevent relapse, especially during the transition from (partial) inpatient to outpatient care. BRIDGE is a programme for activating older patients with multiple illnesses and depressive symptoms. It follows a (partial) inpatient treatment. Patients in geriatrics, gerontopsychiatry, neurology or internal medicine can take part in the programme. Basic and intensive versions are offered depending on the severity of depressive symptoms. The programme focuses on establishing positive activities and habits in everyday life and the targeted promotion of physical activity. The aim of the project is the stabilisation of the treatment results of the (partial) inpatient stay. In addition, the programme aims to reduce depressive symptoms and inpatient treatment days. BRIDGE also aims to promote physical activity, quality of life and the well-being of patients. 

For more information on the study, please visit the BRIDGE website or follow the link below:
https://innovationsfonds.g-ba.de/projekte/neue-versorgungsformen/bridge-behaviorale-und-koerperliche-aktivierung-fuer-multimorbide-aeltere-patient-innen-mit-depressiven-symptomen-beim-stationaer-ambulanten-uebergang.626
conditions: Depressive symptoms in multimorbidity in old age

interventions.name:
Intervention group (basic and intensive version):
BRIDGE is carried out by the BRIDGE team according to a standardised, modular treatment manual for behavioural and physical activation in the intervention group. In a stepped care approach, a basic and an intensive version are offered demand-driven,

Control group:
Patients in the control group will receive standard care. In the control group, the outcome, process and health economic evaluation of BRIDGE will also be carried out. For the outcome evaluation, primary data on the primary and secondary endpoints will be collected at five time point

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
(Partial) inpatient stay in geriatrics, gerontopsychiatry or internal medicine, neurology/geriatric centre, living at home, Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS-15) ≥4 points, Mini Mental Status Test (MMST) ≥20 points, multimorbidity, level of care <5, indication for behavioural and physical activation, statutory health insurance, capacity to consent
Exclusion criteria:
Living in a nursing home, illness leading directly to death
